CHAPTER 4: SPATIAL PHYSICS, BOUNDING COLLISIONS & GRAPH CYCLES

1. Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB) Collision Mathematics

In corporate front-end land, developers drop nodes onto a canvas and let them overlap each other like a pile of dirty laundry. Then they try to solve it with heavy force-directed graph physics libraries like D3-force or cytoscape.js that chew through 80% CPU running iterative simulated annealing loops just to push two boxes apart.

In lib_bejson_HTML_bejson_validator_diagram.py and diagram_cli.py (lines 133-149), Elton implements deterministic Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB) spatial physics with $O(1)$ evaluation time per pair: 

SIZE_CLASSES = {
    "small":  {"w": 100, "h": 100},
    "medium": {"w": 200, "h": 100},
    "large":  {"w": 300, "h": 150},
    "huge":   {"w": 600, "h": 300},
}

def get_box_of(shape: dict) -> dict:
    d = SIZE_CLASSES.get(shape.get("sizeClass", "medium"), SIZE_CLASSES["medium"])
    cx = shape.get("cx", 300)
    cy = shape.get("cy", 200)
    return {
        "x": cx - d["w"] / 2.0,
        "y": cy - d["h"] / 2.0,
        "w": d["w"],
        "h": d["h"],
    }

def boxes_overlap(a: dict, b: dict) -> bool:
    return (
        a["x"] < b["x"] + b["w"]
        and a["x"] + a["w"] > b["x"]
        and a["y"] < b["y"] + b["h"]
        and a["y"] + a["h"] > b["y"]
    )

Notice how clean this is: coordinates on the board are anchored at the center point (cx, cy). The engine translates the center point and sizeClass into an axis-aligned box in 4 arithmetic operations, then runs the Separating Axis Theorem along the orthogonal Cartesian axes. If the projected intervals on both X and Y axes intersect, a collision is flagged.

Furthermore, the layout rules dictate a minimum 40px bounding padding between neighboring nodes. If any two shapes violate this clearance, the validator flags the collision before the diagram is ever sent to the renderer.

2. The 50px Grid Quantization Engine

Look at lines 434-442 in lib_bejson_CMS_diagrams.py: 

raw_cx_val = raw_shape_dict.get("cx")

Why is 50px snapping mandatory?

When SVG renderers draw rectangle borders and orthogonal connector paths on sub-pixel fractional coordinates (like x: 104.3px), the rasterizer has to interpolate fractional alpha values across physical pixels. This causes fuzzy, blurry lines, misaligned connector arrows, and performance degradation during pan/zoom transforms.

By quantizing every node coordinate to 50px boundary multiples, shapes snap into crisp pixel alignment, connectors render with razor-sharp orthogonal lines, and spatial layout mathematics remain purely discrete.

  // Dynamically restacks horizontal columns/zones into a single vertical column
  const territories = (diagram.territories || []).map(t => ({ ...t }));
  const shapes = (diagram.shapes || []).map(s => ({ ...s }));

  if (territories.length >= 2) {
    // 1. Sort territory zones by horizontal center coordinate cx
    const sortedTerrs = [...territories].sort((a, b) => a.cx - b.cx);
    const targetColX = sortedTerrs[0].cx;

    // 2. Associate shapes with their nearest territory zone
    const terrShapesMap = new Map();
    sortedTerrs.forEach(t => terrShapesMap.set(t.id, []));
    shapes.forEach(s => {
      let bestTerr = sortedTerrs[0];
      let bestDist = Math.abs(s.cx - bestTerr.cx);
      for (let i = 1; i < sortedTerrs.length; i++) {
        const d = Math.abs(s.cx - sortedTerrs[i].cx);
        if (d < bestDist) { bestDist = d; bestTerr = sortedTerrs[i]; }
      }
      terrShapesMap.get(bestTerr.id).push(s);
    });

    // 3. Stack zones vertically with a 60px inter-zone gutter
    let currentBottomY = 0;
    const zoneGap = 60;
    sortedTerrs.forEach((t, idx) => {
      const zShapes = terrShapesMap.get(t.id) || [];
      const tSize = t.size || 280;
      const originalTopY = t.cy - tSize / 2;
      const originalBottomY = t.cy + tSize / 2;

      if (idx === 0) {
        currentBottomY = originalBottomY;
      } else {
        const shiftX = targetColX - t.cx;
        const newTopY = currentBottomY + zoneGap;
        const shiftY = newTopY - originalTopY;

        t.cx = targetColX;
        t.cy = Math.round(t.cy + shiftY);

        zShapes.forEach(s => {
          s.cx = Math.round(s.cx + shiftX);
          s.cy = Math.round(s.cy + shiftY);
        });

        currentBottomY = newTopY + tSize;
      }
    });

    // 4. Normalize bounding coordinates with 60px horizontal / 50px vertical margins
    let minX = Infinity, minY = Infinity;
    shapes.forEach(s => {
      const d = SIZE_CLASSES[s.sizeClass] || SIZE_CLASSES.medium;
      minX = Math.min(minX, s.cx - d.w / 2);
      minY = Math.min(minY, s.cy - d.h / 2);
    });
    const normShiftX = 60 - minX;
    const normShiftY = 50 - minY;

    shapes.forEach(s => {
      s.cx = Math.round(s.cx + normShiftX);
      s.cy = Math.round(s.cy + normShiftY);
    });
    territories.forEach(t => {
      t.cx = Math.round(t.cx + normShiftX);
      t.cy = Math.round(t.cy + normShiftY);
    });

    return { shapes, territories };
  }
}

  2. It aligns all zones to a single unified vertical axis (targetColX).
  3. It calculates the cumulative bounding height of Zone 1, inserts a 60px spacer gutter, and drops Zone 2 directly underneath it, followed by Zone 3.
  4. It recalculates connector anchor angles and bounding viewBox coordinates.
  5. It triggers fitView() with a smooth SVG animation.
